conviction_note: The stock trades on the guide (Q2's +15.98% was a miss outweighed by the Q3 guide). US spot HRC has risen another ~$100-130/st since the 23 July guide, which supports a Q4 guide above the $575m Q3 figure and a constructive 2027 reset. Against that sit the Stelco Hamilton idling, Canada's 50% counter-tariff and Stellantis summer pauses. Peer guides and the Wells Fargo upgrade already carry part of the price story, so p_up is 57 on proxies and abs_move is 12 (implied 10.66, own median 14.1). That gives +1.68 scaled against an impact_sum of +2.7; the gap is the proxy discount held in p_up, as the core intends.
bar: Company guide: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA approximately $575m (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm); Q4 'expected to even further exceed' Q3; FY shipments 16.5-17.0Mt, capex ~$700m. EPS consensus is disputed: $0.19 (Tiger/Earnings Agent, 2026-10-12, https://www.itiger.com/news/1150861578) vs $0.24 (Benzinga/The Right Trader) vs $0.25 (Earnings Whispers). Revenue consensus $5.55-5.72bn, also disputed. No sourced EBITDA consensus, so the EBITDA guide is the bar.
positioning_check: No dated September/October FINRA settlement was found (Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503). Last dated figure: 84.5M shares short at the 2026-04-30 settlement, 3.67 days to cover (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/clf/short-interest). Benzinga's sentiment page, updated about 2026-08-10, shows 14.8% of float, rising (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CLF/sentiment). The sweep has MarketBeat at ~15.5% of float and 3.2 DTC, undated. Skew is -15.8 vol pts (25d put IV minus call IV), so upside is paid; put/call OI 0.59. That is a crowded short with the option market leaning up, so negatives are shrunk.

findings.finding: US HRC spot kept climbing through Q3 and into Q4, after CLF set its Q3 guide on 23 July. Nucor CSP was $1,135/st on 20 Jul and $1,145/st on 27 Jul, then rose $10 a week to $1,190 (8 Sep), $1,220 (28 Sep), $1,230 (5 Oct) and $1,240 (12 Oct). SMU's HR assessment was $1,280/st for the week of 15 Oct, +$40 m/m, against $1,165/st on 21 Jul. Spot sits roughly $100+/st above the level the Q3 guide and the 'Q4 further exceeds Q3' language were set on, which points to a Q4 guide well above $575m and supports the ~$500m 2027 contract-reset uplift (2027 EBITDA up to $3.3bn per the July call).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line has driven the large moves: 2026-07-23 +15.98% (Q2 EPS miss, Q3 guide ~2x Q2); 2025-10-20 +21.47%; 2026-02-09 -16.43% on a weak outlook and slipped POSCO timing. The name pays heavily for guidance surprises in both directions.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-20 (page also carries the 2026-10-12 Nucor CSP $1,240/st and the SMU 15 Oct $1,280/st assessment)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Wells Fargo upgrade (6 Oct) cites prices up from $900 to $1,300 and beats in late 2026/2027. But the stock is $12.30, down 5.2% over 5 days and -24% from its 52-week high, below the WF $14 target and roughly at the consensus PT ($11.80-11.96). If the market had priced a Q4 guide materially above Q3, the stock would not be flat over 20 days (-1.6%) while spot rose $40 m/m. The 'Q4 > Q3' language is unquantified, so the number itself is not in the price.
findings.independence: Peer guides on 2026-09-17 point the same way: Steel Dynamics expects higher realised prices with backlog ~50% above prior-year Q3 and extending into Q1 2027; Nucor expects higher mill earnings on price (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/steel-dynamics-issues-q3-2026-guidance-on-record-steel-shipments-and-wider-metal-margins-1479096.htm). Nucor CSP $1,230 on 5 Oct via GMK (https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-has-raised-the-price-of-hot-rolled-coils-to-1-230-per-tonne/). Industry proxy, not a CLF number.

findings.finding: The Q3 quarter is likely to land at or slightly above the $575m adjusted EBITDA guide. The guide assumed ASP +$55/t vs Q2's $1,124/t (about $1,179/t), unit cost -$10/t and shipments >4.3Mt, all set when spot was ~$1,135-1,165/st. Spot then rose through the quarter (Nucor CSP $1,160 on 10 Aug, $1,190 on 8 Sep, $1,220 on 28 Sep), and the spot/index-linked share of the book reprices with a 1-2 month lag, so realised price should come in at or above the guided uplift. Estimated beat about +2% on EBITDA, inside the 'approximately' range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats and misses have mattered less than the guide: Q2 2026 missed EPS (-$0.20 vs -$0.19) and rose 15.98% on the guide; Q1 2026 beat (narrower loss) and fell 2.11% on costs.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly inside what the company guided, so mostly priced; that is why the size is small. The unpriced part is the late-quarter spot climb above the July level, which no published Q3 EBITDA consensus reflects (none was sourced).
findings.independence: Nucor and STLD both guided Q3 mill earnings up on price (2026-09-17). Shares the spot price series with the first finding, but lands on a different line (the reported quarter, not the guide).

findings.finding: US natural gas was cheaper in Q3 than forecast: Henry Hub averaged about $2.78/MMBtu in August 2026 (FRED via MarketXLS), down from $2.89 in July and well below EIA's July STEO Q3 forecast of $3.37. That is a cost tailwind for an integrated BF/DRI steelmaker that took an $80m energy spike in Q1 2026, and supports the guided -$10/t unit cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Costs drove the Q1 2026 print: an $80m energy cost spike, and the stock fell 2.11% (reported 5%+ intraday) despite a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro input, partly inside the guided cost decline; small. Nobody quantifies CLF's energy line in previews.
findings.independence: EIA STEO forecast of $3.37 for Q3 (https://eia.gov:443/outlooks/steo/report/natgas.php). Proxy: CLF has not confirmed its Q3 energy cost.

findings.finding: Stelco (CLF's Canadian segment) is indefinitely idling Hamilton's cold-rolled and coated lines from 9 Oct, with 330-500 layoffs. Stelco's memo says demand for its cold-rolled and galvanized products fell almost 25% in Q2 2026 vs the 2024 quarterly average. Canada doubled its counter-tariff on US steel to 50% from 8 Sep, and the CEO said 'there's no market in Canada for the amount of galvanized steel we produce.' Ottawa (Carney, Joly) threatens legal action over the 2024 takeover commitments. Likely effects: Q4/2027 commentary on Stelco, idle costs, and a dent in the July claim that 'Stelco's improving performance' drives the $3.3bn 2027 figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Canada has hurt before: the Feb 2026 print (-16.43%) cited a sluggish Canadian market. The stock fell to $11.3 in late August on a rumoured US-Canada tariff cut and rose 8% on 5 Oct as Canada-related pressure eased.
findings.why_not_priced: The layoffs were widely covered, so the event is known. The P&L effect is not quantified anywhere (idle costs, mix shift to Lake Erie, any legal provision), and the call will be the first time the company sizes it. Net of the rest: Stelco says steel output will not drop (mix shift only), and the US operations, where the HRC upside sits, are most of EBITDA, so this is sized well below the HRC finding. Shrunk further for the crowded short and upside skew.
findings.independence: Canada 50% counter-tariff from 2026-09-08 (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/canada-doubles-counter-tariff-on-us-steel-to-50-percent-effective-september-8-1473263.htm); BNN Bloomberg 2026-10-08 on layoff notices (https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/company-news/2026/10/08/stelco-begins-issuing-layoff-notices-as-first-job-cuts-set-to-take-effect-sunday). Shares the US-Canada trade breakdown event with the sixth finding but lands on a different line (Stelco volumes vs US pricing protection).

findings.finding: Stellantis, a major Detroit Three customer of CLF auto steel, reported Q3 2026 North American shipments down 12% y/y (-47k to 357k). Planned summer production pauses cut Jeep Grand Cherokee and Compass output by about 25k units each, partly offset by Ram (+17k). GM and Ford Q3 US sales fell 6% and 6.6%. CLF guided about half of its +300kt Q3 volume increase to come from automotive, and Q3 shipments of more than 4.3Mt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto volume disappointment was part of the Feb 2026 -16.43% (the automotive market 'didn't provide a boost').
findings.why_not_priced: Published 14 Oct, after most previews. Comparison is y/y, while CLF's guide is q/q vs a maintenance-heavy Q2, so the transmission is uncertain. Ram pickup (steel-heavy) was up. Proxy, sized small, and shrunk for positioning.
findings.independence: GM/Ford Q3 sales down 6%/6.6% (https://www.dbusiness.com/daily-news/stellantis-sales-tick-up-3-in-q3-gm-sales-down-6-ford-sales-slip-6-6/). Sales, not production. Proxy.

findings.finding: Steel Dynamics guided Q3 on 17 Sep (after CLF last spoke) with record steel shipments, rising realised prices and an order backlog nearly 50% above prior-year Q3, extending through Q1 2027. Nucor guided Q3 EPS to $5.55-5.65 vs $4.84 adjusted in Q2, with steel mills up on higher prices. This is order-book evidence that flat-rolled demand and pricing hold into Q4/Q1, which supports CLF's Q4 guide and its leverage in 2027 contract talks (non-auto talks conclude late Nov/early Dec).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As the first finding: the guide line has moved this stock +16% to +21% and -16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and mostly priced into the sector; the CLF read-through is indirect. Sized small. Nucor's guide was below consensus ($5.84-6.17), so the market may doubt the magnitude of mill margin gains.
findings.independence: Nucor Q3 guide (https://finviz.com/news/393374/nucor-announces-guidance-for-the-third-quarter-of-2026-earnings). Overlaps the HRC price theme of the first finding, but the evidence here is backlog and order book, not the spot quote.

findings.finding: The US-Canada steel tariff deal (50% to 25% on Canadian steel) that drove CLF's August sell-off to ~$11.3 did not happen. The US imposed Section 338 duties on Canadian goods from 22 Aug, Section 232 duties on Canadian steel stay at 50%, and Canada retaliated on 8 Sep. Import protection for CLF's US mills, the basis of management's pricing and 2027 reset thesis, is intact into the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff headlines move this name: down to $11.3 on the rumoured cut (Aug 26 note), +8% on 5 Oct on tariff tailwinds.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock recovered only to $12.30 from $11.3, still well below the $16.70 high, so the market has not fully restored the tariff premium. The call is where management will state the pricing benefit. Largely public, so small.
findings.independence: Freedom Broker 2026-08-26 on the rumoured cut and sell-off (https://fbroker.kz/en/news/51687-fb-cleveland-cliffs-akciialarynyn-aleueti-20-ga-deiin-kk-2); Quiver 2026-10-05 on renewed tariff focus (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Cleveland-Cliffs+gains+as+investors+refocus+on+tariff+tailwinds+and+upcoming+earnings). Shares the trade-war event with the Stelco finding, but they sit on opposite sides of the border and both can be true.

findings.finding: No asset-sale or POSCO filing since the Q2 print. EDGAR for CIK 764065 shows only an 8-K item 5.02 (24 Jul), an SD, a 13G and Form 4s since 23 Jul. As of the July call only ~$100m of the ~$425m idled-property sale programme had been received, Toledo HBI offers fell 'short of our value threshold', and POSCO talks had 'made little progress' (the H1 2026 signing target was missed). Long-term debt rose to $7.70bn at 30 Jun from $7.25bn at year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: POSCO timing slippage contributed to the 2026-02-09 -16.43% (shares fell more than 15% as the CEO pushed the timeline).
findings.why_not_priced: Small idled-property sales may not need an 8-K, so the absence of a filing is weak evidence (lesson 5). The question is what the money buys: the proceeds are for deleveraging, and rising HRC EBITDA does that faster anyway. Near zero; filed so the panel can see the POSCO/asset-sale status going into the call.
findings.independence: IndustryWeek 2026-07-27 on $100m received, Toledo HBI and POSCO delays (https://www.industryweek.com/leadership/companies-executives/news/55393737/cleveland-cliffs-sees-much-stronger-second-half-more-growth-into-27).

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded short into a guide-driven print: about 14.8-15.5% of float short (Benzinga ~Aug 10; MarketBeat undated), 84.5M shares at the last dated settlement (30 Apr, 3.67 DTC). The option market pays for upside (25d skew -15.8 vol pts, put/call OI 0.59), and the 5-day run-up is -5.23%. On a guide that is at least in line, short covering adds an upside mechanism; a weak guide meets shorts already positioned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positive guide prints gapped +15.98% (Jul 2026), +21.47% (Oct 2025) and +12.45% (Jul 2025), consistent with short covering amplifying up-moves.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew already prices the upside asymmetry, so this is mostly priced and kept small. The 5-day drawdown into the print suggests some de-risking that a confirming guide would reverse.
findings.independence: Dated FINRA-based 84.5M at 2026-04-30 (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/clf/short-interest). The baseline skew is independent of the short-interest data.

outside_window.finding: 2027 non-automotive fixed-price contract negotiations typically conclude by late November/early December; their final reset level (vs ~$800/t prior-year basis and ~$1,150+ now) settles after the window. Only call commentary lands inside it.
Steel Dynamics reports Q3 after the close on 2026-10-19 and Nucor on 2026-10-26, both after CLF's exit window closes (close of 2026-10-19).

baseline_tension: The evidence leans up, in line with the upside-paid skew (-15.8) and the crowded short, so it agrees with the option market rather than beating it. That is why p_up stays at 57 rather than higher; the 5-day -5.2% drift is the one piece of the tape that leans the other way.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Stelco/Canada finding -1.0 to -0.7. Stelco says output is unchanged and the US mills carry the HRC upside.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, upside skew): Stellantis auto-volume negative -0.6 to -0.4.
Lesson 5 ('no filing' is not a cause): asset-sale/POSCO absence finding -0.3 to -0.1, since small property sales need no 8-K.

Lesson 3/duplicate check: peer-guidance finding +0.5 to +0.4, because it overlaps the HRC price theme; Stelco and tariff-deal findings checked as two lines of one event, not a contradiction, and both kept.
Lesson 6: bar confirmed as the company's $575m EBITDA guide. EPS consensus disputed ($0.19/$0.24/$0.25), so nothing is sized on EPS.
